mechanism: Images differ in CUDA toolkit and headers; kernels that JIT at load (DeepGEMM, Triton) depend on them.
summary: Verda 1H200.141S.44V image (2026-10-04): nvcc 12.8, so vLLM 0.30's DeepGEMM JIT asserts (needs >= 12.9) and FP8 must run with VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0; python3.12-dev missing, so Triton's launcher build fails until it is installed. Nebius gpu-h200-sxm image (2026-10-05): nvcc 13.0, DeepGEMM JITs, driver 580.173.02 (Verda 580.126.09); clocks lock at 1980 MHz on both. Open observation: plain vLLM BF16 (not batch-invariant) matched the batch-invariant reference exactly on Nebius at concurrency 128 (18,602/18,606 answers, KL 0.0), but on Verda at concurrency 32 diverged on 466/490 MMLU-Pro answers; the reference itself reproduced across both venues. Cause not isolated (venue/driver vs concurrency).
title: GPU venue images: Verda H200 image lacks DeepGEMM-capable nvcc and Python.h; Nebius H200 image has nvcc 13.0
triggers: choosing a GPU venue for FP8 work
plain BF16 at concurrency 32 vs 128 on one VM
